key_insight: RXNGraphormer can be independently reproduced and remains effective on external reaction-prediction benchmarks, but its performance drops in heterogeneous or distribution-shifted settings. In short, it is reliable in familiar conditions, yet less robust when the data differs from training.
problem_solved: This paper evaluates whether a reaction prediction model is truly reproducible and whether it generalizes beyond the original benchmark to real-world external datasets. It addresses the gap between reported model performance and practical transferability.
method: Independent reproduction of RXNGraphormer results to verify experimental consistency.
Evaluation on external benchmark datasets to test cross-dataset generalization.
Analysis of model behavior under heterogeneous and distribution-shifted reaction settings.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides evidence that benchmark success can translate to reproducible results, but also highlights the need to test models under diverse, real-world conditions. It is especially useful for teams deploying reaction prediction systems where dataset shift is likely.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram showing reproduction and external benchmarking pipeline
Side-by-side bar chart comparing performance on original vs external datasets
Heatmap or scatter plot illustrating performance drop under distribution shift
Icon set for reproducibility, transferability, and robustness
paper_title: Reusability report: Assessment of reproducibility and applicability to external datasets for RXNGraphormer
paper_authors: Chonghuan Zhang, Majian Zeng, Qianghua Lin, Kuangbiao Liao
